 STATE OF GUJARAT  Versus  OM ATULBHAI ODEDARA ==========================================================
Appearance:
MR HK PATEL, ADDL. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR VIRAT G POPAT(3710) for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 16/01/2024

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By way of the present petition under Section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the petitioner has prayed to quash and set aside the order dated 31.7.2021 passed by the learned District and Sessions Judge, Porbandar in Criminal Misc. Application No.307 of 2021, whereby the learned Session Judge has granted bail to the respondent - original accused.

2. Learned APP for the petitioner State would submit that on irrelevant consideration, the learned Sessions Court has granted bail to the respondent accused on the ground that the victim and the respondent was in relationship, this is totally extraneous consideration as this cannot be considered in a case where offences under the provisions of the POCSO Act as well as u/s 376 of the IPC are levelled against the petitioner.

He would further submit that there should be some other consideration, which may ignite the learned Sessions Court to exercise NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18306/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined discretion not in case of love relationship between the respondent and the victim.
He would further submit that the victim is aged 15 years and 11 months at the time of commission of the offence and it is established on record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is submitted that the learned Sessions Court has committed error in granting bail to the accused.

3. On the other hand, learned advocate Mr. Virat Popat for the respondent accused has placed on record marriage certificate and would submit that the victim and the accused are married to each other on 4.12.2023 and therefore, cancellation of bail would disturb their married life and thus, he submits to allow this petition.
4.

Having heard learned advocate appearing for both the parties and having gone through the reasons and findings recorded by the learned Sessions Court in Criminal Misc. Application No.307 of 2021, this Court is not approving such reasons for granting bail.

This Court is failed to understand that how the Special POCSO Court can record reason that since the victim is aged 15 years and 11 months and she has love affairs with the respondent accused and therefore, without discussing merit of the case, the bail should be granted.

The very findigns and reasonings are against the scheme and object of the POCSO Act, but considering the aspect that now the victim is married with the respondent accused and cancelling the bail would disturb their married life, no case is made out to cancel the bail of the respondent accused, as supervening circumstances favours the respondent accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18306/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/01/2024 undefined

At this juncture, this Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of XXX Vs. Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and another reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 718.
5.
